checked_sources: Antony et al., arXiv:2402.18984, total-burning section and Theorem 5.7
correctness.rationale: For any graph \(H\) with at least two vertices, \(b(H)=2\) exactly when some vertex has at most one nonneighbor. For a vertex-node \(v\) in \(T(G)\), the nonneighbor count is \((n-1-d(v))+(m-d(v))\); connectivity rules out the only case with one missing neighbor but no nonincident edge, forcing \(v\) to be universal and leaving at most one edge not incident with it, i.e. a star or star plus one leaf-edge. An edge-node has at least \(n-2\) nonneighbor vertex-nodes, so it gives only \(n\le3\), already contained in the listed families. Sufficiency is immediate, and the consequence for \(b(G)=2\) follows from the published bound \(b(G)\le b_T(G)\le b(G)+1\).
residual_risks: The auxiliary Graph Atlas stress test described in the record had no verifier path in the inspected package; correctness does not rely on it.

value.rationale: This is a complete structural classification of the first nontrivial value of a recently studied graph invariant and exactly resolves the equality split inside the natural \(b(G)=2\) layer. Its short proof does not make the boundary arbitrary.

final_claim: For every connected finite simple graph \(G\) of order at least two, \(b(T(G))=2\) exactly when \(G\) is a star or a star with exactly one added edge between two leaves; consequently these are exactly the graphs in the layer \(b(G)=2\) for which total burning does not increase the burning number.
limitations: Only the first nontrivial total-burning layer is classified.
The result does not classify equality \(b_T=b\) for larger burning number.
